rules: built is the implementer's report; review is set only by the owner.
Subjective presentation gets an owner-picked visual target (labelled fixture studies) before it spreads to other artifact kinds.
Fixture evidence proves rendering only. W0/W7 rows need live runs with the real agent across varied questions; never the same question twice, never a stand-in page presented as the feature.
The agent writes artifact code; the sandboxed frame is the boundary. Checks only help it repair (load/runtime errors, size, deadlines).

Agents have no catalog limits (owner, 2026-11-17): they write TypeScript and invent their own components and rendering; no fixed schema, projection catalog or pre-built renderer stands between them and the page.
out_of_scope_here: Artifact browser / Ratatui-derived thread list (icons, left rail, status hierarchy): another session owns it

contracts.scene-artifact-envelope: A theorem-artifact part with artifactKind "scene" carries, as its payload, exactly the theorem-scene-v1 payload a theorem-scene part carries (contractVersion, sceneId, title, fallbackText, packageHash, scenePackage). The UI reads it as the same scene; a theorem-scene part with the same packageHash beside it is not listed twice.
contracts.frame-contract-mount-options: mountRenderers(table, { bare, fills }): a bare renderer draws the whole reply surface (no card); a renderer that fills takes the whole panel body.
contracts.app-npm-imports: A bare import outside the App's import map resolves to https://esm.sh/<spec>?target=es2022&external=react,react-dom, fetched by the person's browser while it builds the App and bundled in; root-relative and relative paths inside fetched modules resolve against esm.sh. A fetch failure is a build problem: 'Could not fetch <url> from npm: ...'.
contracts.app-npm-types: The check's first pass names the bare imports nothing declares (TS2307); each is looked up with a HEAD to its esm.sh module URL, and the X-TypeScript-Types entry and every declaration file it reaches are put under /npm/<host><path> with their specifiers rewritten to those paths, the specifier mapped by compilerOptions.paths; the second pass checks against them. No header, or esm.sh unreachable: declare module '<specifier>'.
